Finite Nehari / rational-candidate API¶

These helpers are finite-dimensional teaching and validation tools for SISO Nehari/AAK-style workflows. They sit above the C++ finite-Hankel primitives and is not a full infinite-dimensional AAK or Nehari solver.

Typical workflow¶

import lattice_dsp as ld

criteria = ld.FiniteNehariCandidateCriteria(
    max_tail_error=1e-3,
    max_rational_error=1e-2,
    max_pole_radius=0.99,
)

candidates = ld.finite_nehari_rational_candidates(
    tail,
    ranks=[1, 2, 3, 4],
    rows=48,
    cols=48,
    criteria=criteria,
)
selected = ld.select_finite_nehari_candidate(candidates)

The returned candidate rows include the finite Nehari diagnostics, fitted rational denominator/numerator, poles, rational tail response, and an accepted flag.

High-level finite-section reducer¶

finite_aak_reduce_tail wraps the candidate workflow and optionally attaches a finite Schmidt-pair certificate for the selected rank. This is the current high-level finite-section SISO AAK/Nehari workflow. It is useful for tutorials and controlled experiments, but it is still not a full infinite-dimensional Hardy-space solver.

result = ld.finite_aak_reduce_tail(
    tail,
    ranks=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    rows=48,
    cols=48,
    criteria=criteria,
)

print(result["selected_rank"])
print(result["selected"]["poles"])
print(result["certificate"]["schmidt_left_residual"])

For an actual stable lattice/IIR model, use finite_aak_reduce_iir. It computes an impulse response internally, runs the same finite-section candidate workflow, and returns the reduced numerator, denominator, and reflection coefficients when stable.

iir_result = ld.finite_aak_reduce_iir(
    reflection,
    numerator,
    ranks=[2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8],
    n_impulse=192,
    rows=96,
    cols=96,
    criteria=criteria,
)

print(iir_result["selected_rank"])
print(iir_result["reduced_reflection"])
print(iir_result["relative_impulse_error"])

Finite AAK/Nehari certificate¶

For a more AAK-shaped diagnostic, use finite_aak_siso_certificate. It computes the finite Hankel SVD for a chosen target rank, reports the first neglected singular value, verifies the finite Schmidt-pair equations, and attaches the rational candidate for the same rank.

certificate = ld.finite_aak_siso_certificate(
    tail,
    rank=3,
    rows=48,
    cols=48,
    criteria=criteria,
)

print(certificate["sigma_next"])
print(certificate["schmidt_left_residual"])
print(certificate["schmidt_right_residual"])
print(certificate["candidate"]["poles"])

This is still a finite-section certificate rather than a full infinite-dimensional Hardy-space AAK/Nehari solver, but it makes the singular-vector target and the rational candidate explicit.

Exact validation case¶

A tail of the form

\[\gamma_n=\sum_{i=1}^r c_i p_i^n,\qquad |p_i|<1,\]

has finite Hankel rank at most r. The finite_nehari_exact_rational_tail.py tutorial uses this fact as a controlled validation: ranks below the known order are rejected, while the correct rank recovers the poles and tail to near numerical precision.

Reference¶

Finite-dimensional Nehari/AAK helper routines.

These helpers sit above the C++ finite Hankel primitives. They are intended as small, inspectable building blocks for tutorials and experiments, not as a claim of full infinite-dimensional Nehari or Adamyan–Arov–Krein optimality.

The main workflow is:

  1. approximate an anticausal tail with finite_nehari_approximate_tail;

  2. fit a scalar recurrence to the Hankelized tail;

  3. select the first rank that satisfies user-chosen error and stability limits.

class lattice_dsp.nehari.FiniteNehariCandidateCriteria(max_tail_error=0.001, max_rational_error=0.01, max_pole_radius=0.99)[source]¶

Bases: object

Selection thresholds for finite Nehari/rational SISO candidates.

Parameters:

  • max_tail_error (float) – Maximum relative error between the original anticausal tail and the Hankelized finite Nehari approximation.

  • max_rational_error (float) – Maximum relative error between the original tail and the fitted rational recurrence realization.

  • max_pole_radius (float) – Maximum allowed modulus of the fitted recurrence poles. Values below one indicate a stable causal realization of the fitted tail model.

max_tail_error: float = 0.001¶
max_rational_error: float = 0.01¶
max_pole_radius: float = 0.99¶
lattice_dsp.nehari.finite_hankel_matrix_from_tail(tail, *, rows, cols)[source]¶

Return the finite Hankel matrix generated by an anticausal tail.

tail[n] is placed on anti-diagonals so that H[i, j] = tail[i + j]. This is the finite-section object used by the Nehari/AAK teaching helpers.

Parameters:

  • tail (Any)

  • rows (int)

  • cols (int)

Return type:

ndarray

lattice_dsp.nehari.finite_aak_siso_certificate(tail, *, rank, rows, cols, criteria=None)[source]¶

Build a finite-section SISO AAK/Nehari diagnostic certificate.

This routine is the first “true AAK/Nehari” bridge in the package: it uses the Schmidt-pair equations for the finite Hankel matrix directly. For a chosen target rank r, it reports the first neglected singular value sigma_next, verifies the finite Schmidt-pair identities

H v = sigma_next u and H.T u = sigma_next v,

and attaches the existing finite Nehari/rational candidate for the same rank. It is still a finite-section diagnostic, not a full infinite Hardy-space AAK/Nehari solver.

Parameters:

  • tail (Any)

  • rank (int)

  • rows (int)

  • cols (int)

  • criteria (FiniteNehariCandidateCriteria | None)

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

lattice_dsp.nehari.fit_rational_tail(tail, order)[source]¶

Fit a scalar recurrence/IIR model to a tail sequence.

For a sequence g[n] generated by a stable rational model, there are coefficients a_1, ..., a_p such that

g[n] + a_1 g[n-1] + ... + a_p g[n-p] ≈ 0.

This routine estimates the recurrence by least squares and returns a scalar IIR denominator, numerator, and poles. It is a practical finite-data rational bridge, not a standalone AAK solver.

Parameters:

  • tail (Any)

  • order (int)

Return type:

dict[str, ndarray]

lattice_dsp.nehari.finite_aak_reduce_tail(tail, *, ranks, rows, cols, criteria=None, attach_certificate=True)[source]¶

Select a finite-section SISO AAK/Nehari rational reduction candidate.

This is the highest-level finite-section helper in the current package. It evaluates several finite Nehari/rational candidates, selects the first one that satisfies the supplied accuracy and pole-radius criteria, and optionally attaches a finite Schmidt-pair certificate for the selected rank.

The routine is intentionally named finite_aak_* rather than aak_reduce_iir. It is a finite-section SISO diagnostic/reduction workflow built from Hankel matrices, Schmidt-pair checks, and rational recurrence fitting. It is not a full infinite-dimensional Hardy-space AAK/Nehari solver.

Parameters:

  • tail (Any)

  • ranks (Iterable[int])

  • rows (int)

  • cols (int)

  • criteria (FiniteNehariCandidateCriteria | None)

  • attach_certificate (bool)

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

lattice_dsp.nehari.finite_aak_reduce_iir(reflection, numerator, *, ranks, n_impulse, rows, cols, criteria=None, attach_certificate=True)[source]¶

Reduce a stable SISO lattice/IIR model with the finite AAK workflow.

This helper applies finite_aak_reduce_tail() to the causal impulse response of a stable SISO lattice/IIR model. The selected rational tail model is returned as numerator/denominator coefficients and, when stable in scalar lattice coordinates, as reflection coefficients.

Parameters:

  • reflection (Any) – Reflection/PARCOR coefficients of the full stable SISO denominator.

  • numerator (Any) – Numerator coefficients of the full SISO IIR model.

  • ranks (Iterable[int]) – Candidate rational orders to evaluate.

  • n_impulse (int) – Number of impulse-response samples used for the finite-section problem.

  • rows (int) – Finite Hankel dimensions. The impulse response must contain at least rows + cols - 1 samples.

  • cols (int) – Finite Hankel dimensions. The impulse response must contain at least rows + cols - 1 samples.

  • criteria (FiniteNehariCandidateCriteria | None) – Candidate acceptance thresholds. If omitted, conservative defaults are used.

  • attach_certificate (bool) – Whether to attach a finite Schmidt-pair certificate for the selected rank.

Return type:

dict[str, Any]

Notes

This routine is still finite-section and diagnostic. It is useful for stable SISO IIR experiments, but it is not a full infinite-dimensional AAK/Nehari solver.
